title: Candidate Retrieval Quality Preflight
summary: P3D1 adds explicit read-only Eval and Pack-eval observations. P3D2 consumes the same fresh guards only inside its DB-only activation operation; a valid artifact is not automatically a quality-approved active generation.

api.request: No query parameters or paths. Authenticate and perform the same project-scoped DB lookup as inspection before route or filesystem access. Unknown and denied jobs both return 404.
api.response: shin.server-response.v1 contains shin.preparation-preflight.v1. HTTP 200 means an observation exists, not that it passed.
api.admission: Preflight and ordinary inspection share one process-local nonblocking admission slot. Busy requests receive 503/preparation-inspection-busy. No additional prepared artifact is loaded by a waiting request.
api.inspection: The existing inspection endpoint and shin.preparation-inspection.v1 retain their seven structural checks and do not execute quality suites. Both endpoints share candidate validation, descriptor ownership and final rechecks.

result.structural: The unchanged job, seven checks, artifact_snapshot_id, artifact_bytes and candidate_verified describe the structural observation. candidate_verified may be true while quality fails or is not configured.
result.profile_check: state=not-assessed/passed/failed/unavailable with errors and warnings counters, null before a completed check. Strict Core profile-check runs before the suites. Invalid profile policy prevents both suites from running.
result.quality: eval and pack_eval each contain state, total, passed, failed, query_total, query_passed and resource_check. Counts are null before execution or when a suite cannot be evaluated. Executed empty suites contain zero counts and state=not-configured. Eval query counts include variants; Pack query counts are zero because its assertions are case-level. No query text, case identifiers, source content, paths or raw exceptions are returned.
result.resource_check: Native Server dev39/Core dev22 adds policy, ok, failed_queries and warning_queries to executed eval observations. It remains null for unassessed/unavailable suites and Pack. Strict is default; explicit profile advisory changes admission for only the three work ceilings, never quality, freshness or safety. Resource ok remains false on exceedance or empty eval, independently of suite state. Knowledge health exposes the same counter-only object. See retrieval-evidence-v1 queryRobustnessEval.resourcePolicy.
result.project_quality_assessed: True only when both nonempty suites actually ran in this invocation, whether they passed or failed. This narrow field concerns configured retrieval goldens only, not all project gates.
result.quality_passed: True only when strict profile-check and both nonempty suites passed. Empty, malformed, unavailable and skipped suites never count as success. Generic bootstrap profiles are not exempted.
result.preflight_passed: candidate_verified AND quality_passed after end-of-observation guards. No caller may reuse this boolean as a durable publication token.
result.activation: activation_supported=true and activation_ready=false remain unconditional. This endpoint never changes the active reference, prepares an artifact, creates a lock, repairs, deletes, audits or updates a ledger row; mutations_performed=false.
result.negativeEvidence: Stable candidate-eval-* and candidate-pack-eval-* reason codes distinguish not-configured, failed and unavailable. candidate-profile-failed/unavailable identify the profile policy gate. Structural failures retain existing inspection codes. Successful earlier observations are not erased by later drift.
result.observation: started_at and finished_at describe the server UTC interval. Worktree source is not atomically frozen. A passing observation is neither a signed receipt, deployment proof nor reusable currentness claim.

execution.ownership: Core owns profile case validation, query matching, ranking, expected paths, coverage, budgets and serial/parallel Pack identity. Server only orchestrates shared typed APIs and projects bounded counters. No stdout interception or second ranker.
execution.nativeApi: src/profile_quality.h exposes SuiteEvaluation, evaluate_profile_cases(RetrievalSession&) and evaluate_pack_cases(RetrievalSession&). Both use the provided session and its immutable snapshot. The APIs themselves do not claim freshness or execute project tools.
execution.candidateAdmission: Require a prepared bound artifact, matching ledger and route, healthy strict Doctor, exact current source and matching base before evaluating suites. Otherwise quality remains not-assessed.
execution.generation: Eval and Pack-eval share one loaded GeneratedSnapshot owner while holding the candidate lifetime read lock and existing Core publication read lock. No filesystem fallback to another generation is allowed.
execution.finalGuards: Exact source comparison runs after both suites. Recheck base, configured project/profile/state identity, lifetime lock, artifact identity and manifest, and the scoped ledger input before accepting the observation.
execution.authority: These are executed tests of Shin retrieval against profile-owned expectations. They do not execute JUnit, Gradle, Playwright, a shell, application code or external services; discovered product tests remain source-observed.
execution.malformedProfile: The shared native evaluation path enforces the same bounded case validation as CLI Eval and Pack-eval. Unavailable diagnostics are intentionally compact; an authorized operator may run the explicit profile-check/eval/pack-eval CLI against the candidate for detailed investigation.

resourceBounds.suites: Existing Core limits apply: at most 128 Eval cases and 256 base-plus-variant executions, and 32 Pack cases. Every Pack case uses the existing bounded serial and parallel identity comparison.
resourceBounds.response: Fixed check set plus two counter summaries; failure detail cannot grow with source text or the number of failed cases.
resourceBounds.memory: One additional candidate snapshot is bounded by retrieval.max_generation_bytes and per-file limits. Parsing, regeneration and query scratch memory are separate; this is not a total process RSS cap.
resourceBounds.time: Profile and input bounds limit work, but there is no hard wall-clock deadline. Preflight is explicit and more expensive than inspection or warm retrieval. No automatic background preflight or cached quality success.
